articleTitle: Analysis of median filter
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Median filters introduced by Tukey found application in image processing. Several authors have considered the statistical and deterministic properties and have discussed some methods of analyzing. However, median filter being nonlinear is not assessable to standard analysis technique. In this paper a new method of characterizing such filter through matrix operator is introduced. A new parameter 'column sum' is extracted. from median matrix. The column sum leads to bring out to prediction of several features of signal like trends (maximum/minimum) monotonic behaviour and periodicity.

articleTitle: An adaptive control system modelled as finite state machine
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive control system based on several different control algorithms. The basic idea is to detect several events of the current variations of the controller error variable, to adjust the parameters of a conventional controller. The adaptive control system uses a state and event driven adaptation strategy. The second aspect of this paper outlines a systematic approach to develop, implement and describe adaptive control systems taking into consideration the demands of real time systems. In this case, state graphs and Petrinets are used as appropriate tools for graphical representation of the adaptive control strategy and the total system. The state graphs describe a finite state machine which can be performed by means of a special digital control loop. The architecture of this digital control loop is a hierarchical control structure, subdivided into an operating block and a supervisor.

articleTitle: A loop based method for distribution power flow solution
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper reports on a new technique for the power flow solution of distribution system. The power flow problem is formulated by writing simple loop equations and representing loads as complex impedances. Solution techniques have been presented for balanced and unbalanced radial networks and also for networks havind radial as well as meshed lines. The proposed method is computationally eeficient, storage economic and free from convergence problem.

articleTitle: A fast algorithm for coherency identification and dynamic equivalencing of power systems
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: An analytical method to decompose a power system into a number of weakly interconnected areas and further to identify the coherent machine groups in each area is presented in this paper. The proposed method is based on a technique of grouping related elements of the network. The system decomposition and coherency groupings obtained is independent of the location of the faults to be simulated in the system. The first part of the algorithm of decomposing the system into weakly coupled areas uses only the information about the transfer admittances between the generator internal nodes. For the subsequent part of identifying the coherent groups of machines in each area, transfer admittances and moments of inertias of the machines are used.

articleTitle: A general method for power flow analysis n MTDC systems
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper presents a novel and general approach for the power flow analysis in multiterminal DC systems. A major feature of this approach is the clear demarcation of the controller and the DC network equations which enables the consideration of a variety of converter controls. The method can also handle the constraints on several variables such as DC current (lD), converter control angle(0) and off nominal tap ratio(a).

articleTitle: Degradation of metal oxide surge arresters under simulated natural conditions
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: The degradation of metal oxide surge arresters (MOSA) under continous operating voltage (C.O.V) with time, is a well known fact. But the contribution of transient overvoltages in the form of lightning surges, switching surges etc.-against which the arrester is used as a protection device, to the arrester degradation has not been studied much. The simulation of a situation, wherein the arrester is kept uder C.O.V and different surges are applied on it, is somewhat complex. A method for simulation of field operating conditions of an arrester in the laboratory is presented in this paper. Results of two seperate degradation studies on different samples under A.C, and D.C. excitations with superimposed transient stresses are given. A comprison of observed data with calculated ones is also made.

articleTitle: Distribution feeder reconfiguration - heuristic algorithms and their performance
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: The problem of feeder reconfiguration has been discussed in this paper. A few heuristic feeder reconfiguration algorithms for radial distribution networks are discussed. Optimum feeder configuration are determined for a test network and the methods. are compared based on these test results.

articleTitle: An optimization approach to the analysis of generalized learning automata algorithms
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Weak convergence methods are used to analyse generalized learning automata algorithms. The REINFORCE algorithm has been analysed. It is shown by an example that this algorithm can exhibit unbounded behaviour. A modification based on constrained optimization principles is proposed to overcome this problem. The relationship between the asymptotic behaviour of the modified algorithm and the Kuhn-Tucker points of the related constrained optimisation problem is brought out.

articleTitle: Series expansion of gaussian-gaussian mixture probability distribution
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper demonstrates that Gaussian - Gaussian mixture (GGM) density function could be conceived as the result of sum of a Gaussian process and a Non Gaussian process which are independent of each other. Expressions for the even order moments of the Non Gaussian process are obtained as a function of the parameters of the mixture distribution. The mixture density function is then expanded in terms of these moments and even order Hermite polynomials. It is shown that first few terms of the series expansion provides reasonably good approximation of the mixture density function. The series representation would lead to simplification of the likelihood ratio function and hence is easier to implement than GGM likelihood ratio receiver.

articleTitle: Programmable signal processor - an ASIC
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Application Specific Integrated Circuits (ASIC's) for digital signal processing applications, are available from several manufactures. However, the fundamental operation of convolution has been neglected for multiple channels and/ or for data lengths greater than 8 bits. This paper describes the architecture of a programmable multichannel convolution ASIC designed and fabricated with 2 micron CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Design and development of controllable filter banks for harmonic current suppression on the AC side of the converters of DC transmission lines
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Elimination of current harmonics on the ac side of converter bridges of dc transmission system has been investigated and reported. This includes characteristic current harmonics at ideally stipulated normal conditions and also the uncharacteristic ones at abnormal conditions particular ly with weak ac system. Suppression of uncharacteristic harmonics is achieved with the use of phase locked oscillator or by firing angle modulation. Furtber elimination is affected via active and or passive filters. Design, control of these and the performance evaluation under changing system conditions and requirements are presented.

articleTitle: PC controlled transistorized pwm inverter for induction motor drive
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Speed control of transistorized PW inverter fed induction motor with selective harmonic elimination and current controlled scheme using personal computer (PC) is described. The whole set of switching angles for eliminating the unwanted harmonies up to 550 Hz while controlling the fundamental corresponding to V/F graph of the machine for constant flux operation, and minimizing the immediate dominant voltage harmonic that will be present in output voltage of the inverter has been presented.The effect of lock-out time an the harmonic spectra,variation of switching frequency of the device, overall block diagram of the drive system with the necessary interfacing cards, their respective function and software realization of the above PWM -schemes have been presented.

articleTitle: Recent advances in queueing networks: a survey with applications to automated manufacturing
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Queueing models have been the most widely used analytical modelling tool for performance studies on complex manufacturing systems. Conventional analysis has proceeded along the lines of product form queueing models, and their extensions. Traditional applications of these models have been restricted to the computation of mean values of important performance measures; besides, certain simplifying assumptions have to be made for these models to be applicable. The last decade has witnessed important advances in the applicability of these tradi tional queueing networks, as well as in newer queueing models that exhibit constructs capable of modelling generic issues arising in a real-life manufacturing system. The issues taken up in this pager are: (i) computation of higher moments of performance measures, besides mean values; (ii) the phenomenon of blocking due to limitations of buffer capacities, and (iii) analysis of a network of multiqueues model of an Automated Manufacturing System. We survey the recent advances in these three modelling issues which are of great importance in the manufacturing context, and present analytical models of Automated Manufacturing Systems incorporating these features. Each model is illustrated with a numerical example.

articleTitle: Design optimization of induction motor
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]

articleTitle: Karnaugh Maps - An artificial intelligence approach
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: The software developed includes an expert system for the simplification of switching circuit expressions with the help of k-maps. The method has been developed for a four variable k-map. The significance of AI becomes clear when we consider the complexities associated with k-maps of higher orders. Since k-maps follow a recursive structure an algorithm developed for a 4 variable k-map can be extended to k-maps of higher orders. The extendability however, entails certain modifications which are not being presented here.

articleTitle: Parallel data compression algorithms
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: The parallel versions of the three data compression algorithms namely i) Block Truncation Coding ii) White Block Skipping iii) Laplasian Pyramid Coding Method were developed and evaluated. The paraIlelizing scheme is applicable to a class of parallel computers. It is shown that the proposed algorithms can be implemented on the existing SIMD computers.

articleTitle: Shape from shading using discrete polynomials
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Given a monocular image, we propose a new method for extracting the shape of objects from the pixel intensities. The problem of solving the partial differential equation corresponding to the reflectance map is reduced to that of solving a finite set of nonlinear algebraic equations. The method involves patchwise approximation of the surfaces in the scene by discrete polynomials. Distinctive features of the method are as follows: a) Shape extraction without initial depth information of any form, (b) Handling of discontinuity (obtained by a zero-crossing operator) by splitting the region into multiple patches around the discontinuities contour and fitting the depth polynomial separately in each patch, (c) Algebraic evaluation of the quadratic polynomial coefficients in the case of identical source and viewer direction, and (d) Facility to integrate stereo information.

articleTitle: Applications of A.I. in control systems
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This Paper Presents a case study of an aircraft central system that can tolerate control surface failures using Semantic control theory. In this application, the semantic control system uses system identification and the control mixer concept to exploit the analytical or control redundancy among the control surfaces and thus accommodate the failures. System identification Is performed using artificial intelligence techniques. With this approach unpredictable faults can also be accomodated, which is normally not realized using the conventional techniques.

articleTitle: Medium range forecasting of power system load by median filtering and walsh transform
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]

articleTitle: Design of a microprocessor based radar tracking system using stepper motor
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper highlights a simple microprocessor based system that uses a stepper motor for the realisation of a radar tracking system. The hardware and software developed describes a two-stage control. In the first stage, the tracking antenna is taken to the position of the Incoming radiation. In the second stage, the antenna is controlled to align itself with the position of maximum received radiation within an error of + 1.80 (on the horizontal plans). With a little change in this mechanism the antenna can be made to scan the whole surface above the horizontal plane and to point to any position thereof. The tracking procedure was performed by the microprocessor and expected results were obtained within some limitations.

articleTitle: Postprocessing of spectral output of EEG signals for display of long records
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: In this paper, a linear predictive (LP) analysis of several segments of EEG data is performed and the spectral information in condensed form is displayed as position of three major peaks of smoothed LP spectrum versus time. A zero-crossing analy sis of the EEG record is also performed frame by frame so as to get a rough estimate of major frequency component in each segment. A comparison of curves of major frequency component versus time obtained by the above two methods shows a close sim ilarity between the two displays. The displays provide EEG data in a convenient condensed form for a clinician and also helps in the classification of EEC. by computer pattern recognition techniques.

articleTitle: Multi-objective stochastic optimal thermal power dispatch
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: The paper treats non-commensurable objectives such as operating cost, minimal emission and minimum transmission line losses in optimal thermal power dispatch systems using a method which also includes uncertainties and inaccuracies in the system date. The method considers the randomness of system production cost, NOx emission and transmission line loss coefficients via the variance of generator output. Using specific method of reducing it to a deterministic model, a multiobjective optimisation problem is formulated. /spl epsi/-constraint method is used to generate non-inferior solutions, alongwith the trade-off function between conflicting objectives. Interaction with the decision maker to access the indifference band is obtained via the surrogate Worth Trade off method and the utility approach. Surrogate Worth function also provides the optimal trade-off value, from where optimal solution is obtained. The validity and effectiveness of the method has been demonstrated by analysing a 6-generstors system.

articleTitle: An iterative approach to pattern recognition
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]

articleTitle: GNU-Aid: Intelligent computer aided instruction system
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Educational applications of computer technology have been under development since the early 1960s. These applications have included scheduling courses, managing teaching aids, and grading tests. The predominant application, however, has been to use the computer as a device that interacts directly with the student. This has led to the evolution of Intelligent Computer Aided Instruction System (ICAI). This paper discusses the various components of an IGAI system and explains the GNU-AID SYSTEM. GNU-AID is an ICAI system which incorporates artificial intelligence techniques to help the student learn the GNUEMACS editor (enhanced version of EMACS on UNIX). Its logical and inferencing capabilities are derived by simulating the execution of the solution specified by the student.

articleTitle: A knowledge representation paradigm for multiple expert systems
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: The expert system technology has grown to a level where expertise of single expert is found inadequate to tackle complex problems. Recently the focus of research has now been oriented towards methodologies in which several expert systems can cooperate and communicate for solving common complex problems. This paper investigates a knowledge representation paradigm for building multiple expert systems. The main features of the proposed methodology include blackboard architecture, control engine and meta knowledge. The objective of the system is to acquire the knowledge from one or more domains and put it at workplace of appropriate expert system. The system is capable of conflict resolution, consistent advice and complex problem solving. In this paper, we illustrate a model, knowledge representation scheme and control inference.

articleTitle: Artificial neural net based noise cancellor
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper presents a new method for noise cancellation with an Artificial Neural Network. The network used is a feedforward one with three layers. The backpropagation and Stastical Cauchy's learning algorithms are employed for adaptation of the internal parameters of the network. The constrained tangent hyperbolic function is used to activate the neurons and to provide the desired non-linearity. Promising simulation results for noise cancellation intensify the validity of superseding the proposed scheme for many existing techniques. To demonstrate the effectiveness, the proposed method is applied to different, input conditions with varying SNRs. With incomplete signal samples the net is found to produce output having a striking resemblance with that of the desired ones. A performance comparision of the two algorithms is presented in the paper for better appraisal.

articleTitle: A new technique to separate the non stationary component of a signal and its application in biomedical engineering
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Several algorithms to separate nonstati- onary part of a signal are presented in this work. In the autoregressive model both end prediction (prediction using N/2 pastValues) and midprediction filters are used. If the nonstationary part consists of random impulsive waves of low occurance rate it may be separated as error signal corrupt with 'carried over' errors. Two schemes, signal inversion and time-reversal, are proposed to remove this corruption. Impulses with slowly rising and falling edges are recovered better by the mid-prediction filter because it intro duces a pair of complex conjugate zeros on the frequency axix.

articleTitle: An improved version of fdlf suitable for systems with large voltage variations
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper presents a new version of Past Decoupled load flow (FDLF) which is suitable for systems with large voltage variations. This version differs from the standard one In a way the branch resistance is considered in B' and B" matrices. The branch resistances are neglected while forming the B'matrix in standard version of FDLF. This paper shows that if the resistance is considered in both B' and B" matrices the method converges faster than the standard version for systems with large voltage variations. The convergence of this new version is affected by suitable choice of convergence factor. It is found that a convergence factor of 0.9 for reactive power model makes the model still faster. The performance of this model is demonstrated by taking examples of networks of different kinds including actual utility networks with wide voltage variations. To achieve the large voltage variations in normal systems, their loads are increased by different P/sub F/ and Q/sub F/ factors. The test results reveal that the proposed version supercedes other versions for such networks.

articleTitle: A higher order parallel abstraction for fixed degree divide and conquer problem solving strategy
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: In this paper, we present an algorithmic framework for the Fixed Degree Divide & Conquer(FDDC) problem solving strategy, that adapts the divide and conquer algorithm for parallel computations. We capture the notion of a thread of execution in an active task object which are instances of a data type called the tasktype and propose a higher order, tasking abstraction called maptask that takes as its arguments, a tasktype, the (fixed) degree of the runtime task hierarchy and the arguments for the tasks. We have implemented the above abstraction by extending C with task-type and maptask in a package called the CT Kernel that currently executes tasks in a distributed environment consisting of 10 netwoked VAXstations. Using the above abstractions we have implemented the FDDC algorithms for mergesort, FFT, Cubic spline based curve fitfing, Fractals, Matrix multiplication, as well as Iterative relaxation.

articleTitle: Virtual shared memory interconnect bus provides real-time linkage between multiprocessors
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Recent advances in computing and processor technology have brought mainframe computing power to the desktop. While these advances have radically changed the general purpose computing market, they are only beginning to be seen in the real-time market. Real-time distributed systems have been relying on raw computing power to satisfy performance requirements. Scalable multiprocessor architectures, while providing substantial processing power, do not often meet the demands of deterministic applications such as real-time simulation and control. The need for concurrent data sharing in multitasking, multiprocessor systems is the bottleneck in utilizing these technologies. This paper defines the architecture of an interfacing system for efficient coupling of processing modules for high performance multiprocessor applications. The Virtual Shared Memory Interconnect (VSI) minimizes data Stency between processors and provides process transparent communication for applications requiring shared data and cross-coupled interrupts between CPUs. This permits attainment of maximum available CPU bandwidth and brings a truly scalable architecture to the real-time arena. A commercial implementation of a 64-bit RISC CPU for real-time applications, configured around the VSI, is also describecd.

articleTitle: Performance study of cache based multiprocessor designs
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Multiprocessor system are envisaged for use in applications requiring high computing power, fault tolerance, and time critical areas. Designs of such system are qualified using modeling and simulations. The development of an analytical model for a cache based multiprocessor system is presented in this paper. The system behaviour is approximated with a semi-Markov process, and using the model, various performance measures are found out. The results are compared with simulations.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Factors Affecting the Performance of Controller Designed for Robot Manipulators using the Theory of Variable Structure Systems
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: For the evaluation of factors which affect the performance of controllers designed for robot manipulators using the theory of Variable Structure Systems (VSS), control torques, reaching time, chattering and control parameters are suggested as primary indices. A new control algorithm is developed, the results are simulated and compared with the previously developed control algorithms for position control experiment on two link robot manipulator.

articleTitle: Nonlinear system parameter identification - A modified Kalman filter algorithm
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: A modified Kalman filter for parameter identification for non-linear system involves linearization, as there is no direct method available In literature. The extended Kalman filter algorithm for continuous system parameter identification given by authors [3] is applicable to nonlinear continuous system parameter identification by linearizing about the equilibrium points utilising Jacobian matrix method, Effectiveness of the desired algorithm has been illustrated by a second order example of Rayleigh's equation[6].

articleTitle: Pade extended prony (PEP) model reduction for linear multivariable systems
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: In this paper we develop a general idea of Pade.ex tended Prony (PEP) modelling which reduces to the classical Pade and.(extended) Prony models as special cases. The formulation includes development of PEP models based on min /spl par/ /spl dot/ /spl par//sub 2/ norm ( in the classical sense) and a new min /spl par/ /spl dot/ /spl par//sub 1/ norm (in the robust sense).

articleTitle: Design and implementation of matrix algorithms of systolic array processor
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Design and implementation of two impor- tant matrix operations namely matrix multi plication and matrix Inversion using geo metric arithmetic parallel processor (GAPP) array is described. These matrix operations are implemented oh an IBM PC/XT compatible with an add on card con sisting of two GAPP clips. Together, these two clips have an array of 12 X 12 processing elements. The implementation is done using GAL - GAPP algorithm lang uage. Performance evaluation shows that this idea can be extended to large arrays.

articleTitle: Time varying filter for doppler synthesis
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Time companding of broad band signals or doppler shifts of sinusoidal signals can be interpreted as linearly time varying delay. For any stationary signal, a linear time invariant filter can always be designed to generate a prescribed delay using minimum mean square error criteria . A FIR filter of order 2m is sufficient to generate any delay with zero mean square error for signal consisting of m sinusoidals. The coefficients of such a filter are derived by solving normal equations. By using time varying delay parameter for estimation the solution of normal equation generates time varying filter coefficients. This fiIter produces appropriate doppler shifts. Here an expression is derived for the filter coefficients. The performance of the filter is evaluated by comparing the correlation of the signal with the doppler shifted signal.

articleTitle: Multi-channel planar filters
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper deals with the notion of planar filters. These are approximate inverses of polynomial functions of finite degree. One obvious variatior presents itself when the function is a matrix, this leads to approximate left and right inverses. The other variation we introduce is based on norm criterion on the nature of approxima tion. We develop what is more familiar as Planar least square inverse ( PLSI ) filter and introduce the notion of Least absolute deviation inverse ( PLDI ) filter. based - /spl par/ /spl dot/ /spl par//sub 2/ and /spl par/ /spl dot/ /spl par//sub 1/ norm minimization of the error in linear maxtrix equation AS = B.

articleTitle: Real-time signal processor: ADSP2100 based
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: The task of building signal processors for real-time applications has always been, one involving a trade-off between factors like processing throughput & hardware flexibility. The designer is thus constrained to optimize his system from one of the above angles. DSP processors that have recently hit the market have offered flexible real-time capabilities to the system designer. Two hardware configurations using the ADSP 2100 chip for real time signal processing is presented.

articleTitle: An adaptive controller for megawatt frequency control
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: In power system operation and control applications, for which adaptive controllers are increasingly seen to be a potential successors to the traditional PID controllers a major aspect of the control problem is the elimination of the offset. In the present paper an adaptive controller is presented for megawatt frequency control to completely eliminate the offset when the system is subjected to a large distuibance. The effectiveness of the proposed controller for considering the generation rate constraints and parameter variations has also been shown.

articleTitle: A self-routing photonic switch using an optical content addressable memory
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: A novel self-routed slot-switching scheme using an integrated optic directional cou, ter is outlined using apulse interval coded optical content adressable memory (PICOCAM). The in tegrated optic devices required for its implementation are also out lined. Yhis bit-switching approach avoids the bottleneck in speed imposed by the electronic drive circuitry in electrooptic switches.

articleTitle: Real time simulation of microprocessor based multi-area tie line power controller
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper reports on the development of microcomputer aided realtime simulation of three utilities by three motor-alternator sets which are interconnected via tie lines. The utilities are considered as separate areas supplying their own loads and in addition power transfer takes place between them as per the need of power situation without violating the priori contracts. This can be treated as very useful training simulator in man-power development.

articleTitle: Source localization in a wedge shaped shallow sea
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper looks into the problem of localization of an acoustic source in shallow sea with a sloping bottom as found in the continental shelf area. A vertical array of sensors, either floating or secured to the sea bottom, is used to receive the acoustic signals from the source including those travelling by different paths. First, a spectral matrix of the array signal is computed and it is then subjected to eigenvalue decomposition. The space spanned by the eigenvectors is partitioned into two subspaces, namely, a signal subspace spanned by the eigenvector corresponding to largest eigenvalues and a noise subspace spanned by the eigenvectors corresponding to repeated eigenvalues. The signal subspace is also spanned by a linear combination of direction vectors corresponding to all multipaths These two subspaces are orthogonal. We exploit this property of orthogonality in the estimation of range, bearing and depth of a source. Some of the significant findings are as follows:(1) Unlike in the flat bottom channel it is now possible to measure the bearing with respect to upslope or downslope direction.(2) The azimuth scan shows a sharp peak at the correct location for steep slope(>1/spl deg/) (3) A study of finite data effect has shown that the background generally remains unchanged as the number of snapshots increases. However, the signal peak amplitude increases roughly at the rate of 3dB per doubling of the number of snapshots.

articleTitle: A simulation of fiber distributed data interface for token ring lan protocols
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: The aim of this work has been to graphi cally simulate the protocols employed for 100 Mbps token ring local area network (LAN), using the fiber-optic medium, known as Fiber Distributed Data Interface (FDDI), and to study its performance evaluation. In the computer based simulation, the effort has been made to describe the working of the protocols using graphical, dynamically working models. Also performance characteristics, such as Throughput Vs Token rotation time, Throughput Vs Ring Latency, Throughput Vs Data Arrival Rate are obtained. The asynchronous priority level throughput for different data arrival times are tabulated. From the characteristics, it is found that the relative difference between the ring latency and the token rotation time (TRT) has a significant effect on the maximum total throughput. Also with the higher value of the TRT the throughput increases faster compared to lower TRT values.

articleTitle: Neural Network Approach to Pisarenko's Harmonic Retrieval Method
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Pisarenko's Harmonic Retrieval (PHR) Method Is Perhaps The First Eigenstructure Based Spectral Estimation Technique. The Basic Step In This Method Is The Computation Of The Eigenvector Corresponding To The Minimum Eigenvalue Of The Autocorrelation Matrix Of The Underlying Data. This Eigenvector Is Obtained As The Solution Of A Constrained-minimization Formulation. In This Paper, We Recast This Constrained Minimization Problem Into The Neural Network (NN) Framework By Choosing An Appropriate Cost Function (or Energy Function) For The NN. We Also Present The Theoretical Analysis Of The Proposed Approach For The Asymptotic Case. It Is Shown That The Minimizers Of The Energy Function Are The Eigenvectors (with A Given Norm) Of The Autocorrelation Matrix Corresponding To The Minimum Eigenvalue, And Vice Versa. Further, All The Minimizers Of This Energy Function Are Also Global Minimizers. Results Of Computer Sirntilations Are Presented To Support Our Analysis.

articleTitle: Binary image compression using the radon transform
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: A new technique for compression of binary images is proposed. The Radon transform is used to convert a binary image to a set of 1-dimensional (1-D) non-binary sequences, which are coded using 1-D techniques. A binary image can be reconstructed from a very small number of projections and this leads to significant compression. The compression ratio for a binary image of size NxN is inversely proportional to N.

articleTitle: Estimation of voltages and currents due to lightning strokes to transmission lines
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper presents an improved equivalent circuit representation for the lightning stroke to estimate the magnitudes and waveshapes of current 's and voltages through transmission system components due to lightning strokes. Results indicate that arrester currents can go as high as 130kh with a front time of the order of 15us' while the arrester potentials are substantially rectangular lasting anywhere upto 60 US. Transformer potentials are initially oscillatory exceeding the BIL. This could be dangerous. Thus, this work was successful in improving the equivalent circuit representation of the lightning stroke and highlighted interesting areas for further research.

articleTitle: Tutoring system for circuit theory with passive elements
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]

articleTitle: VLSI implementable neural network for solving linear programming problems efficiently
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: An adaptive algorithm is proposed for solving the Linear Programing problems using Neural Networks. The LP-solver circuit structure Is designed which can implement the adaptive algorithm. The advantages of the proposed LP-solver have been discussed along with the simulation results supporting the claims.

articleTitle: Case studies in modelling cooperative knowledge systems
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Understanding cooperative knowledge systems is becoming a central issue in Al research. The questions centre around complexity of management of separate knowledge sources In terms of heterarchical and hierarchical organisation structures, and convergence of planning and design cycles. In this we discuss two cases: maintenance planning and VLSI design. The VLSI design mode-I described here is in the initial stages. The objectives of this ongoing research is to ask questions and attempt to sketch the nature of cooperative problem solving behavior.

articleTitle: Processing of EEG signals for reducing the effects of adjacent activities
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: The primary objective of recording EEG signal at a particular location on the scalp is to know the electrical activity of the brain right below the electrode position. However, signals of cerebral origin from areas beneath adjacent electrodes also gets superimposed on the original signal of Interest. In this paper, we are proposing a least squares technique for estimating the effect of adjacent activities and subsequently subtracting it from the recorded EEG so as to got a better estimate of the activity beneath the electrode of interest. The results show that the processed signal better reflects the activities below the electrode location than the one originally recorded.

articleTitle: Study of lens shaped arrays
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Sensor arrays of different geometric configurations are used in Sonar and Radar to improve the detection performance. Conventional arrays used in sonar are having limited aperture due to the constraints imposed by the dome and the platform in which they are fitted. Cylindrical arrays with circular cross section are the most widely used configuration. However dimensionally these are not the optimal arrays as they fail to fully utilise the extended length of the streamlined dome. A cylindrical array with Iens shaped cross section, a better suited configuration for the dome, provides a wider broaside aperture and increased array gain. In this paper we discuss, the theory of lens shaped arrays and compare their performance with circular arrays.

articleTitle: A simulator study of recovery of HVDC links following AC system faults
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper presents the simulator study of a two-terminal HVDC system. The various AC system faults to which the study system is subjected are a) remote-three-phase ground fault, b)single-phase-ground fault and c)threephase-ground faults. These faults are applied both at the rectifiey and inverter ends. The results of the simulator study are presented to demonstrate the controller performance in the recovery of HVDC link following AC system faults.

articleTitle: Design of maxflat fir filters
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: An optimal design method for MAXFLAT FIR filters is proposed hare. A polynomial mapping approach is used to search the optimal order of filter and required flatness at w=O and W=/spl pi/. Explicit expressions for computation of to-efficients of low pass filters are tried here. The algorithms to transform low pass co-efficients into high pass, band pass and band rejection are proposed.

articleTitle: Corrective Rescheduling to Alleviate Bus Voltage Violations
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of alleviating bus voltage limit violations. The voltage violations are removed by obtaining the PV-bus voltage corrections. The model is in terms of incremental variables and utilises sensitivity coefficiente. Linear set of coordination equations is obtained for getting optimal PV-bus voltage corrections so as to alleviate bus voltage violations.

articleTitle: Adaptive coding and optimal speech storage in digital speech interpolation systems
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: One of the important issue in speech interpolation is that of speech freeze-out which becomes a very serious consideration with multihop networks. The paper discusses the implementation of two such techniques namely speech storage and variable bitrate strategies with their independent and combined effects on the performance of multihop, DSI networks. The trade-off between the effective increased channel capacity and the degradation of the speech quality has also been pointed out. The basic architectural configuration of the system using multimicroprocessor system has been discussed and the potentialities of the method in accomodating newer versions of coding algorithms at desired speed of response have been included.

articleTitle: Walsh transform based digital protection of power transformer
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: The problem of protection of power transformers against abnormal conditions such as faults etc. has been of great concern to the protection engineers. Traditionally, percentage differential relaying scheme has been used to protect the transformer against internal faults, even though this relaying scheme may mal operate due to various reasons such as magnetizing and overvoltage inrush currents. The proposed relaying scheme incorporates the magnetizing inrush current as well as overvoltage inrush phenomena due to switching for the purposes of blocking only. The fundamental, second-harmonic component caused by magnetizing inrush current and the fifth harmonic current caused by voltage inrush have been realised using digital filter based Walsh transform because of its immunity to slight frequency variations and also because of accuracy. The relaying scheme which uses the concept of unit protection has been designed, fabricated and tested using 8086 CPU as the main processor.

articleTitle: Unipower II - architecture and design of a loosely coupled multiprocessor system
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: UNIPOWER II, a loosely coupled multiprocessor system designed in Computer Group, can support maximum of four processors according to the needs of application. It provides a standard UNIX environment for easy development/ porting of applications, better performance, cost effectiveness and modular growth. Present version of UNIPOWER II conforms to UNIX V.3.1 and provides many popular BSD extensions and Network protoclos. This paper can be divided into three parts. First part ts an In troduction to loosely coupled and tightly coupled architectures. Second part deal with UNIPOWER II architecture, Configurability, operating enviornment. Final part gives a design note an various modules involved In the development of UNIPOWER II.

articleTitle: Process Management System
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: In this paper a novel concept towards process management is suggested. Mathematical modelling and simulation techniques have been used to understand the process. Simulation is also used in closed loop controls as in case of self tuning regulator. As simulation gives better insight into the process, it is extremely useful in the design and tuning of control systems. In many cases instrument failures and/or cable faults cause plant shutdown. A parallel case of plant and simulator enables the operator to conduct optimisation study and control loop tuning. Simulated model of process would be working as a hot standby process. The model takes process parameters through the same data highway which is used by process control computer. Al techniques can be used where online testing of new control techniques can be performed on simulator and parameters can be passed on to process control computer.

articleTitle: Simulation of a data flow computer
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: A data flow computer architecture achieves hitgher computing speeds than the traditional von Newmann architecture by exploiting software parallelism at the instruction level in a highly parallel system of processing hardware. Data flow architectures executs- data flow graphs - directed graphs in which nodes represent instructions and interconnecting arcs define data flow oaths. One such data flow architecture, the Manchester Data Flow Computer has several rings which communicate via a common switch. This pacer describes the simulation of a single such ring. The code is written in Modula-2 using object oriented techniques. Partial cerformance figures obtained by the author's group are also presented. The paper concludes by suggesting several simulator enhancements.

articleTitle: Contraction and related mappings: theory and applications
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: This paper discusses the theoretical aspects of contraction and related mappings and their application to certain systems engineering problems. It is demonstrated how the fixed point property of contraction mappings can be exploited to establish sufficient conditions for the stability of a class of nonlinear systems, as also to generate the actual output of the system to a given bounded input. Use of contraction and modified contraction methods for the iterative solution of sets of nonlinear algebraic equations is discussed. Numerical examples are given, and applications to Control and Power Systems problems cited and described

articleTitle: Digital flight control - scenario for the 90's
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: In the last decade, considerable progress has been made in the sphere of aircraft control. The arrival of powerful and reliable microprocessors has encouraged their usage for the Implementation of different control laws. Those processors are configured redundantly to achieve a high degree of reliability for fall-safe operation. This paper highlights the evolation of the concept of digital flight control, a few case studies, as well as Issues Involved in the design of such a system . Mention of some of the contemporary implementations and prospects for the future is also made.

articleTitle: Data/voicenideo integration on fiber distributed data interface
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: The Fiber Distributed Data Interface (FDDI) is a 100 megabit per second (Mbps) Local Area Network that uses Optical Fiber as the medium. It provides both the high bandwidth and low latency needed to match the capacity of future personal computers. Hence it is expected to become the preferred local area network systems of the 1990s. The FDDI protocol is based on a timed token ring access method. In this paper, we propose a media access control protocol for combined Data/Voice/Video services on FDDI. The most important service requirement for the packetized Voice and Video is the transport of this data with tolerable delays. Ile effect of multiple Voice and Video channels on the asynchronous data traffic and the capacity to handle these services on FDDI is investigated by means of simulation methods.

articleTitle: Power system fault diagnosis using artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: ACE '90. Proceedings of [XVI Annual Convention and Exhibition of the IEEE In India]
abstract: Fault detection and diagnosis in real-time are areas of research interest in knowledge-based expert systems. Rule-based and model-based approaches have been successfully applied to some domains, but are too slow to be effectively applied in a real-time environment. Neural computing is one of the fastest growing areas of artificial intelligence research. This paper explores the suitability of using artificial neural networks for fault detection and diagnosis of electric power systems. The paper describes a neural network design and simulation environment for real-time fault diagnosis of a model power system.
